sources.title: Complete multipartite graphs and Braess edges
sources.inspected: Existing independently inspected pinned source/domain notes, page-marked text pp13-19, and current primary publisher/repository records.
sources.notes: Known: general twin-edge update, no-dominating-vertex case, minimum-size-two case, sufficiently-large-p result, and equal non-singleton part sizes. Conjecture 3.4.7 predicts no Braess graph when there are at least three non-singleton parts and dominating vertices. Remark 2 compares sign polynomials for two non-singleton parts; its displayed equation (13) has a transcription defect, so our derivations use Theorem 3.2.3 instead.

sources.title: Kemeny's constant and Braess cliques in graphs
sources.authors: Jane Breen, Emma deBlieck, Kevin N. Vander Meulen
sources.inspected: Current primary HTML passages and existing pinned independent source review.
sources.notes: Theorem 3.5 gives the general independent-twin clique update through accessibility, size and degree. Theorem 4.7 specializes to complete bipartite graphs. Section 5 already shows that the signs of individual edges do not determine the sign of a clique addition. These formulas and generic phenomena cannot be claimed as new. The inspected results do not state an all-r minimum-part sign theorem with dominating vertices.

sources.title: Edge addition and the change in Kemeny's constant
sources.inspected: Primary publisher abstract and section previews only.
sources.notes: The stated main results optimize the change from adding an edge to a tree. This is relevant prior edge-design work but does not itself establish the multipartite claims. Full-paper equivalence assessment was not performed.

sources.notes: The search engine labelled this recently published, but the primary title page is 2021. The Kemeny chapter studies twin pendent paths. It was not treated as a 2026 resolution or reviewed in full.

claim.statement: The bounded searches have not identified a primary publication proving the exact prospective all-r minimum-part theorem or general strict part-size ranking. This is not evidence of exhaustive novelty; both candidates need mathematical review and further priority assessment before publication claims.

impact_boundary: A correct result for ideal complete multipartite networks does not establish gains for sparse, weighted, congested, or measured real networks. Those require a separate justified model and evaluation.
